title: Why It's Okay To Be Weird
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that staying calm as a teacher does not mean suppressing one's natural personality, and that embracing one's quirks and idiosyncrasies actually makes teachers more effective. He offers three reasons: being genuinely oneself is more interesting to students than a stoic, over-controlled demeanor; authentic self-expression is inherently more inspiring than a performance of someone the teacher isn't; and students distrust teachers who project a manufactured perfection, sensing the dishonesty even if they can't articulate it. He observes that many naturally funny, warm people change dramatically the moment the school day begins, adopting a cold perfectionism that may suppress misbehavior but forecloses a genuinely happy classroom culture. Linsin closes by encouraging teachers, whether introverted or extroverted, storyteller or quiet motivator, to simply be themselves without apology.
points: Staying calm does not require suppressing personality; embracing one's natural quirks makes a teacher more effective, not less.
Students are drawn to genuine uniqueness and find over-controlled, stoic teachers less interesting and less engaging.
Authentic self-expression is inherently more inspiring than performing a version of oneself that isn't genuine.
Students sense manufactured perfection as dishonest, which undermines trust even when the demeanor seems polished.
A cold, perfectionist persona may temporarily suppress misbehavior but prevents a genuinely happy, well-behaved classroom culture.
quotes: It doesn’t mean you must dampen your enthusiasm or become a robot when you step in front of your students.
Students are drawn to uniqueness, to teachers who are unabashedly themselves. They want to be around them, learn from them, and follow where they lead.
There is no passion in trying to be someone you’re not. You can fake it, but there will always be something missing.
Students don’t trust teachers who put on a show of perfection in their demeanor, manner, tone, and style.
It’s not uncommon for bright, funny, lovely people to change drastically the moment the morning bell rings.
Just being you, on the other hand, embracing your weird and wonderful self, unapologetically, is your greatest strength.
